verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug is likely present in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). SQLite developer Dan found and fixed it on 2026-03-03
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed ... 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09) ... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) was withdrawn and its planned features moved to 3.53.0 (2026-04-09). 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) shipped the WAL-reset fix
verdicts.evidence: changes.html: '2026-03-06 (3.52.0) Withdrawn ... features ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; 3.51.3 and 3.53.0 entries both say 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE was added in SQLite 3.8.8 (2015-01-16). PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP were added in 3.51.0 (2025-11-04)
verdicts.evidence: 3.8.8 log: 'Added the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE option'; changes.html 2025-11-04 (3.51.0): 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, added in 3.16.0 (2017-01-02), disables the close-time checkpoint
verdicts.evidence: changes.html 2017-01-02 (3.16.0): 'Added the SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE option to sqlite3_db_config().'

verdicts.claim: By default SQLite checkpoints automatically when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB) and when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: checkpoint 'occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection ... closes'; 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x ... PASSIVE at min-checkpoint-page-count (default 1000), every checkpoint-interval (default 1m), TRUNCATE at truncate-page-n (default 121359)
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m # Default', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', v0.5.15 passive-first, logs 'passive checkpoint skipped'; how-it-works: 'long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing'

verdicts.claim: The Rails SQLite3Adapter DEFAULT_PRAGMAS (main branch) set journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL and journal_size_limit=67108864 (64 MB)
Tailscale reported 19 SQLite database corruptions over about six months, starting with a corrupted backup flagged in August 2025
verdicts.evidence: GIGAZINE: 'problems began in August 2025 when database corruption was reported in the S3 backup. There were 19 database corruptions in six months ... limited to control plane configuration data'; tmstmpvfs shim logs led to fix. Secondary sources only (Tailscale primary unfetched, per draft).

verdicts.claim: Phil Eaton's reproducer (2026-08-23) is about 100 lines of C ... two threads and three connections ... 1 GiB mmap_size ... on 3.51.2 lost writes; 3.53.0 none
verdicts.evidence: Eaton: 'About 100 lines of C', 'two threads and three database connections', 'PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824', builds amalgamation-3510200 vs 3530000, 'database disk image is malformed', 3.53.0 'you'll stop seeing these lost writes'

verdicts.claim: former SQLite engineer Scott Perry called it a 'Top three data corruption bug of my career'
verdicts.evidence: Tsai quoting Scott Perry: 'I spent the last two years of my time working on SQLite ... Top three data corruption bug of my career for sure'
